campaignTrail_temp.questions_json = [ { "model": "campaign_trail.question", "pk": 1, "fields": { "description": "January 16, 2008: We knew we weren't at an advantage there, but the results from the Michigan primary are worse than expected. Barack Obama was shot and killed while leaving a campaign event in Elko, Nevada. The country is in shock, the details remain confused, and every camera in America is waiting for more information. How should we proceed?" } }, { "model": "campaign_trail.question", "pk": 8, "fields": { "description": "February 4, 2008: The affair allegation has broken into the open. Edwards denies it completely and accuses hostile media organizations of attempting to destroy the Democratic frontrunner. Someone in his campaign is talking, but nobody knows who yet. At least it may take a little wind out of Edwards's sails."}},{"model":"campaign_trail.answer","pk":2,"fields":{"question":1,"description":"“I want to broaden the message. "}},{"model":"campaign_trail.answer","pk":8,"fields":{"question":2,"description":"“I do not want to turn mourning into political theater. I will release a brief statement, offer my condolences, and otherwise stay out of the cameras.”","feedback":"The statement avoids exploitation, and right now that's probably what's most important."}},{"model":"campaign_trail.answer","pk":9,"fields":{"question":3,"description":"“Everything stops for at least a week. The campaign loses momentum, but earns trust."}},{"model":"campaign_trail.answer","pk":10,"fields":{"question":3,"description":"“We should honor the suspension, but I also want to speak directly to our supporters online. "}},{"model":"campaign_trail.answer","pk":11,"fields":{"question":3,"description":"“Campaign activity should stop, but our movement cannot disappear. "}},{"model":"campaign_trail.answer","pk":14,"fields":{"question":4,"description":"\"There can be no justice without peace and no peace without justice. Mike makes sense ideologically. If you want somebody in the Oval Office every bit as enthusiastic as you are about smashing the military-industrial complex into pieces and setting it on fire, you found him. He endorsed you almost immediately after Senator Obama's assassination, and there's no question he believes in what we're trying to do.

His r\u00e9sum\u00e9 would be the envy of plenty of sitting Democratic senators, and the man hasn't held elected office in nearly thirty years. He read the Pentagon Papers into the Congressional Record, served in the Army, and his conviction on the war is second to none. Of course, he's also 78 years old and has a habit of turning that conviction into some pretty spectacular rants. Being a veteran helps. Some.

If we win, Mike could make an excellent Vice President. If we lose, there's about a 100% chance picking Mike Gravel had something to do with it. A ticket can probably survive one candidate as ideologically forceful as you are. Two is a harder sell. If you really think you can make it work, go right ahead. Just don't say you weren't warned.

",candidate_score:0.98}, 32:{first_name:"Barbara",last_name:"Lee",party:"Democrat",state:"California",image_url:"https://i.imgur.com/sNSghNK.png",description_as_running_mate:"

Barbara is a lot like you, Dennis, and you already know that \u2014 the two of you are friends and have spent years fighting a lot of the same battles in Congress. There's a personal kinship there, too. You know what it was like growing up poor enough that your family sometimes lived in a car; Barbara escaped an abusive relationship as a young woman and spent time homeless while raising two boys. Neither of you came to these issues from a think tank.

Her lone vote against the Authorization for Use of Military Force was enormously controversial, but after everything that followed, she makes it easy for us to argue that this is the ticket that got it right the first time. She could energize Black voters and women, and nobody would miss the historical significance of putting a Black woman one heartbeat from the presidency. Of course, that includes Americans who aren't entirely comfortable with a Black woman having that much power.

Barbara would make an excellent Vice President and probably be one of the easiest people on this list for you to actually govern alongside. She's from California, though, which won't help us geographically unless we're getting absolutely massacred. And however well you two understand each other, voters still have to accept a ticket this liberal, this anti-war, and this far outside what they're used to seeing.

",candidate_score:1.00}, 33:{first_name:"Ron",last_name:"Paul",party:"Republican",state:"Texas",image_url:"https://i.imgur.com/WQBdV9Q.png",description_as_running_mate:"

I cannot stress enough how bad of an idea I think this is. Look, I get it. You two are practically kindred spirits when it comes to challenging the war machine, the Federal Reserve and the political establishment. Put the two of you in a room together and I'm sure you could find institutions to abolish until sunrise.

Yes, Paul built a remarkable following in the Republican primaries. He also didn't win a single primary or caucus. His libertarian philosophy is nowhere near the mainstream, he wants to eliminate the income tax, and then we have to explain his positions on civil rights to Democratic voters. And if you were hoping for somebody young to balance the ticket, Ron is almost 73.

I understand the appeal of calling this a bipartisan ticket. The problem is that we'd first have to convince the people who nominated you that putting a Republican libertarian on the ticket isn't a repudiation of half the things they voted for. Maybe there's a strange new coalition hiding out there. If you pick Ron, Dennis, we're going to find out the hard way.

",candidate_score:0.97}, 34:{first_name:"Deval",last_name:"Patrick",party:"Democrat",state:"Massachusetts",image_url:"https://i.imgur.com/q3QNLrL.png",description_as_running_mate:"

Deval Patrick is the current Governor of Massachusetts, and he's considerably more moderate than you are. He also took over from Mitt Romney, so if the Republicans nominate that shitbag, having somebody on the ticket who knows his record firsthand could come in handy. Deval doesn't have an enormous national profile yet, but party leaders would breathe a lot easier with him beside you.

There's an obvious complication after Senator Obama's assassination. Picking a Black running mate will invite accusations that Deval is some kind of token replacement for Obama rather than somebody chosen on his own merits. Not picking a Black running mate carries risks of its own, though, especially when so many Black Democrats are wondering what happens to the coalition Obama was building.

Deval gives us youth, executive experience and a bridge back to Democrats who are still nervous about you. But you'd have to meet him halfway. If you select him and then spend the fall running exactly the same campaign you would have run with Mike Gravel, we're wasting the whole point of the pick. If you're prepared to tack toward the center a little, he's a solid choice.

",candidate_score:1.03}, 35:{first_name:"Janet",last_name:"Napolitano",party:"Democrat",state:"Arizona",image_url:"https://i.imgur.com/HSCBKSZ.png",description_as_running_mate:"

Janet Napolitano has an impressive r\u00e9sum\u00e9, Dennis. She's the sitting Governor of Arizona, she has executive experience, and putting her on the ticket would shut up a lot of moderate Democrats who are desperately looking for an excuse to feel good about voting Democratic in November. As painful as choosing somebody this moderate may be for you, it might be what it takes to win.

She's pragmatic \u2014 some people would say to a fault \u2014 and she's perfectly willing to work with conservatives when she thinks it'll get something done. Moderates call that bipartisanship. Some people in our base are going to call it betrayal. Either way, nobody is going to mistake Janet for somebody you picked because she agrees with you about everything.

And there's the other problem: she's not going to keep her concerns to herself. If you choose Janet and then spend the fall frightening every swing voter she was supposed to reassure, eventually she's going to tell you so. If you can live with that, she gives this ticket credibility in exactly the places where we need it most.

Grainy footage from the 2007 Democratic debate shows you acknowledging that you once saw an unidentified flying object at Shirley MacLaine's home. It cuts to several unconventional proposals and then to black: “DENNIS KUCINICH. PRESIDENT?” Cable news is looping it. What do you say?`,[ '“Well, I did see one. It does not mean it was from outer space. It was unidentified, and that makes it a UFO. That is all I ever said.”','“You know, more Americans have seen UFOs than approve of the Bush administration.”','“I saw something I could not explain, and UFO was the best word I had for it. There were other witnesses too. They can corroborate what happened.”','“This is ridiculous. Anyone who watches the debate clip can watch the rest of what I said. Beyond that, I am not spending a financial crisis discussing a light I saw years ago.”' ],['You are technically correct, which is precisely the problem. The campaign has now spent another news cycle explaining the definition of UFO. For a conventional nominee this might be trivia; for you it reinforces doubts voters already have.','The line is funny and Democrats repeat it all day. }; const VP_NAMES={ gravel:"Mike Gravel",lee:"Barbara Lee",paul:"Ron Paul", patrick:"Deval Patrick",napolitano:"Janet Napolitano" }; const OPP_NAMES={ romney:"Mitt Romney",mccain:"John esc=s=>String(s??"").replace(/[&<>"']/g,c=>({"&":"&","<":"<",">":">",'"':""","'":"'"}[c])); function vpKey(){return String(k.democraticVp||"gravel").toLowerCase();} function oppKey(){return String(k.republicanNominee||"mccain").toLowerCase();} function gopVpKey(){return String(k.republicanVp||"").toLowerCase();} function vpName(){return VP_NAMES[vpKey()]||"your running mate";} function oppName(){return OPP_NAMES[oppKey()]||"the Republican nominee";} function gopVpName(){return GOP_VP_NAMES[gopVpKey()]||"the Republican running mate";} function num(v){v=Number(v);return Number.isFinite(v)?v:0;} function purity(){return Math.max(num(k.kucinichPurity),num(k.progressiveTrust));} function ideologicalLeft(){ const p=purity(); if(p>=7)return true; if(p>=5 && ["gravel","lee","paul"].includes(vpKey()))return true; return false; } function resultsTable(){ return [...document.querySelectorAll("table")].find(t=>{ const s=t.innerText||""; return /Electoral Votes/i.test(s)&&/Popular Votes/i.test(s); }) || [...document.querySelectorAll("table")].find(t=> [...t.querySelectorAll("td,th")].some(c=>/Electoral Votes/i.test(c.textContent||"")) ); } function parseResults(){ const table=resultsTable(); if(!table)return null; const rows=[...table.querySelectorAll("tr")].filter(r=>r.querySelectorAll("td").length); const parsed=[]; for(const r of rows){ const cells=[...r.querySelectorAll("td")].map(td=>(td.textContent||"").trim()); if(cells.length<2)continue; const name=cells[0]||""; const ev=(cells[1]&&/^\d{1,3}$/.test(cells[1].replace(/,/g,"")))?Number(cells[1].replace(/,/g,"")):null; const popular=(cells[2]&&/^\d[\d,]*$/.test(cells[2]))?Number(cells[2].replace(/,/g,"")):null; const pct=(cells[3]&&/%/.test(cells[3]))?Number(cells[3].replace("%","").trim()):null; if(ev!==null)parsed.push({name,ev,popular,pct,row:r}); } if(parsed.length<2)return null; const dennis=parsed.find(x=>/Dennis\s+Kucinich/i.test(x.name)); if(!dennis)return null; const surname=String(oppName()).split(" ").pop(); const safeSurname=surname.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g,"\\$&"); let republican=parsed.find(x=>x!==dennis && new RegExp(safeSurname,"i").test(x.name)); if(!republican)republican=parsed.filter(x=>x!==dennis).sort((a,b)=>b.ev-a.ev)[0]; if(!republican)return null; return { kEV:dennis.ev,rEV:republican.ev, kPopular:dennis.popular,rPopular:republican.popular, kPct:dennis.pct,rPct:republican.pct, republicanName:republican.name, table }; } function winTier(ev){ if(ev>=320)return "landslide"; if(ev>=290)return "solid"; if(ev>=270)return "nailbiter"; return "deadlock"; } function vpVictoryLine(tier){ const v=vpKey(), p=purity(); const lead=tier==="landslide"?"And you did it":tier==="solid"?"You did it":tier==="nailbiter"?"And somehow you did it":"You got here"; if(v==="gravel"){ return `${lead} with Mike Gravel beside you, which means voters had every opportunity to decide one Dennis Kucinich was enough and went ahead anyway.`; } if(v==="lee"){ return `${lead} with Barbara Lee beside you, producing a ticket whose opposition to the Bush-era foreign-policy consensus was about as subtle as a brick through a window.`; } if(v==="paul"){ return `${lead} with Republican Congressman Ron Paul on the Democratic ticket. Political scientists are going to be fighting over what exactly that means long after both of us are dead.`; } if(v==="patrick"){ return p>=7 ? `${lead} with Deval Patrick beside you, even though the reassuring young governor never quite managed to sand down the edges of the campaign the way party leaders hoped.` : `${lead} with Deval Patrick beside you, and his presence helped convince nervous Democrats that putting you in the White House didn't require burning the rest of the party to the ground.`; } return p>=7 ? `${lead} with Janet Napolitano beside you. She reassured the center enough to get them through the door; once inside, they discovered you still intended to be Dennis Kucinich.` : `${lead} with Janet Napolitano beside you, and she did exactly what we hoped: reassure voters who liked the idea of change considerably more than they liked some of your ideas for producing it.`; } function vpLossLine(){ switch(vpKey()){ case "paul": return `We always knew asking Democratic voters to put Ron Paul one heartbeat from the presidency was going to make an already tiny needle even harder to thread.`; case "gravel": return `Mike Gravel gave the ticket conviction in industrial quantities. He also gave Republicans about six months of material proving that one ideological insurgent apparently wasn't enough for us.`; case "lee": return `Barbara Lee made the moral argument for this campaign unmistakable. Unfortunately, a lot of voters who respected that argument still weren't ready to put this ticket in the White House.`; case "patrick": return `Deval Patrick gave us credibility with the party center and helped make the ticket look governable. It just wasn't enough to close the sale.`; case "napolitano": return `Janet Napolitano gave every nervous moderate Democrat a respectable reason to vote for you. Quite a few took it. Not quite enough.`; default:return ""; } } function variableWeakness(win){ const anxiety=num(k.voterAnxiety), security=num(k.securityConcern), party=num(k.partySupport), pub=num(k.publicPerception), p=purity(); if(anxiety>=6){ return win ? `Too many voters spent the campaign wondering whether putting you in the Oval Office was a leap into the unknown, but by Election Day that fear no longer outweighed their desire for change.` : `Too many voters never got over the feeling that putting you in the Oval Office was a leap into the unknown.`; } if(security>=5){ return win ? `Your positions on Iraq, Guantánamo and presidential power gave Republicans a real security opening, but they never quite convinced enough voters that restraint meant weakness.` : `Your positions on Iraq, Guantánamo and the Bush administration left enough voters uneasy about national security to give Republicans the opening they needed.`; } if(party<=-2){ return win ? `Half the Democratic establishment spent the campaign supporting you with all the enthusiasm of somebody attending a court-ordered seminar. You won in spite of them.` : `It didn't help that half the Democratic establishment spent the campaign supporting you with all the enthusiasm of somebody attending a court-ordered seminar.`; } if(p>=9){ return win ? `You refused nearly every invitation to sand down the edges. Somehow, voters looked at the full-strength version and decided to take the chance anyway.` : `You refused nearly every opportunity we gave you to sand down the edges. Maybe that cost us the presidency. Nobody can say they didn't know what they were voting for.`; } if(p<=3 && pub>=2){ return win ? `You spent enough of the fall reassuring skeptical voters that the Republican effort to turn you into a frightening caricature eventually stopped working.` : `The cruel part is that you gave ground on some of the things that brought you here, and the voters we were supposed to reassure still didn't come in sufficient numbers.`; } return win ? `God knows the campaign gave Republicans openings, but by the end voters had heard enough of you directly that the caricature never completely stuck.` : `We gave Republicans enough openings that they never had to invent all of the case against us.`; } const OPP_FAIL={ romney:`Romney's entire campaign rested on competence, management and the idea that a private-equity résumé was exactly what a collapsing economy needed. The trouble was that Bain made it awfully easy to ask who his version of competence had actually worked for.`, mccain:`McCain had the biography, the experience and a national reputation for occasionally telling his own party to go to hell. What he never found was a clean way to escape the war, the Republican label and eight exhausting years of George W. Bush.`, perry:`Perry tried to make the election a values-and-confidence contest and came dangerously close to pulling it off. But "Bush the third" was a hard label to shake when the country was already sick of Bush the first two times.`, giuliani:`Giuliani spent months trying to make catastrophe, command and September 11th a complete presidential platform. Eventually voters started asking what President Giuliani planned to do after the emergency briefing ended.`, forbes:`Forbes came out of a convention nobody could control and tried to sell supply-side certainty in the middle of an economic collapse. It was an intellectually tidy argument arriving at almost the worst possible moment.` }; const OPP_WIN={ romney:`Romney found the argument he needed. He sold competence, stability and the promise that somebody who understood business was exactly what the country needed as the economy came apart. Never mind that his record gave us plenty of ammunition; enough voters decided the multimillionaire private-equity guy was somehow the reassuring option. Expect a White House friendlier to corporate America, cautious about dismantling Bush's foreign-policy architecture, and very interested in proving that Republicans can manage the economy without George Bush standing in the room.`, mccain:`That was always McCain's advantage. He could embrace Bush when it helped, distance himself when it didn't, and fall back on a biography that made attacking his character unusually difficult. His administration will probably be more independent than Bush's and less predictable than Romney's, but nobody expecting a sudden retreat from America's military commitments overseas should hold their breath.`, perry:`Perry's campaign was never complicated. He painted you as dangerously liberal, tied every unconventional thing you've ever said into one enormous attack ad and dared voters to gamble on you. His victory is an extraordinary reprieve for the conservative movement after the Bush years; Washington should prepare for tax cuts, deregulation and enough swagger to make the outgoing administration look introspective.`, giuliani:`Giuliani's weaknesses were never difficult to find. His personal life was a tabloid archive, conservatives distrusted him, and his campaign sometimes seemed to consist of saying "September 11th" until somebody changed the subject. But enough voters bought the larger argument about danger and command. A Giuliani administration will likely be socially less conservative than many Republicans wanted and considerably more hawkish than most Democrats feared—a strange coalition held together by tax cuts and the conviction that somewhere, somebody needs to be bombed.`, forbes:`Forbes emerged from a Republican convention that looked ready to tear itself apart and turned being everybody's compromise choice into an advantage. He ran as the businessman-outsider with one overriding prescription for an economy in freefall: lower taxes, simplify everything and let markets breathe. Newt Gingrich will ensure the incoming administration is anything but politically sleepy, and Washington should prepare for four years of supply-side economics delivered by men who regard the Reagan administration as a rough first draft.` }; function popularVoteNote(result,won){ if(!result || !Number.isFinite(result.kPopular) || !Number.isFinite(result.rPopular))return ""; const diff=result.kPopular-result.rPopular; const margin=Math.abs(diff); const fmt=n=>Number(n).toLocaleString("en-US"); if(diff===0)return ` The popular vote ended essentially dead even too, because apparently this election wasn't stressful enough.`; if(won && diff<0)return ` You won the Electoral College while losing the popular vote by about ${fmt(margin)} votes, which guarantees that roughly half the country will spend the next four years reminding you of it.`; if(!won && diff>0)return ` The especially cruel part: you actually won the popular vote by about ${fmt(margin)} votes and still lost the presidency. Welcome to the Electoral College.`; if(won && diff>0)return ` You also carried the popular vote by about ${fmt(margin)} votes, which makes the mandate argument considerably easier.`; return ` ${esc(oppName())} carried the popular vote by about ${fmt(margin)} votes too, so there isn't much of a consolation prize hiding in the national totals.`; } function victoryParagraphs(kEV,rEV,result){ const tier=winTier(kEV); if(tier==="deadlock"){ const paul=vpKey()==="paul"; const alt=gopVpName(); const p1=paul ? `Dennis, you tied. 269–269. After everything that's happened in this election, apparently the country decided the only sensible conclusion was to refuse to pick a president at all. Fortunately, Democrats control enough House delegations that, barring a political earthquake, you're going to become President anyway. Ron is another story: the Senate chooses the Vice President separately, and I wouldn't bet my house on a chamber full of Democrats and Republicans deciding that Ron Paul belongs one heartbeat from the presidency. ${gopVpKey()==="lieberman"?"Let's hope to God they don't throw Joe fucking Lieberman in there.":`The other constitutional option is ${esc(alt)}, which is bad enough. After everything that's happened in this election, apparently the country decided the only sensible conclusion was to refuse to pick a president at all. Fortunately for you, Democrats control the House delegations and have the stronger hand in the Senate. ${vpVictoryLine("deadlock")} Barring a political earthquake, you're going to become President of the United States without actually winning the Electoral College outright. I'm sure this will inspire a calm and thoughtful national conversation.`; const p2=`${esc(oppName())} is furious, and for once I can't entirely blame him. ${OPP_FAIL[oppKey()]||""} Republicans are already calling your incoming administration illegitimate, while Democrats have suddenly developed a passionate reverence for eighteenth-century constitutional procedure. ${variableWeakness(false)}`; const p3=`There is no mandate here. Congratulations, Mr. President. Try not to break anything before inauguration.`; return [p1,p2,p3]; } if(tier==="landslide"){ return [ `Dennis, you didn't just win. You won ${kEV} electoral votes to ${rEV}. Nobody is going to explain that away as a fluke, a third-party spoiler or a few thousand votes in Ohio. ${vpVictoryLine(tier)} Republicans will argue until they're blue in the face about what exactly the country voted for, but with a margin like this you've earned something dangerously close to a mandate. Considering where we started, I hope you'll forgive me for staring at that sentence for a minute.`, `${esc(oppName())} was supposed to be the man who stopped this from happening. ${OPP_FAIL[oppKey()]||""} ${variableWeakness(true)} By Election Day, whatever frightened voters about Dennis Kucinich apparently frightened them less than four more years of Republican government. ${esc(oppName())} is going to have a very unpleasant few months figuring out how his name ended up attached to that verdict.`, `Tomorrow the hard part starts. You've promised peace, healthcare, a different relationship with the world and enough structural reform to keep half of Washington's lobbying firms awake until sunrise. Some of it will happen. Some of it won't. Some Democratic senators are probably already figuring out how to tell you that the thing you promised five minutes ago is unfortunately impossible. But tonight? Forget them. Dennis Kucinich is President-elect of the United States. If that can happen, I'm done telling you what's impossible.` ]; } if(tier==="solid"){ return [ `Well, Dennis, ${kEV} electoral votes to ${rEV} isn't exactly Lyndon Johnson in 1964, but nobody gets to put an asterisk next to your name either. You won clearly, you won nationally, and ${vpVictoryLine(tier)} There's going to be an argument over what kind of mandate you've actually earned—there always is—but you've got enough room to say voters knowingly chose this ticket rather than merely stumbling into it. For a campaign that began with most of Washington waiting for you to drop out, that's not bad.`, `${esc(oppName())} had openings. God knows we gave him openings. ${variableWeakness(true)} But ${OPP_FAIL[oppKey()]||""} In the end, the financial collapse, exhaustion with the Bush years and your stubborn insistence that politics didn't have to look like this proved enough. Republicans will spend the winter arguing that a better nominee could have beaten you. Maybe they're right. Fortunately, they didn't nominate that guy.`, `Don't confuse a convincing victory with an easy presidency. The Democratic Party supported you in November; that doesn't mean every Democrat suddenly woke up wanting a Department of Peace. The people who voted for you are going to expect results, while Republicans are going to treat stopping those results as the first step toward taking the country back. Still, you've got four years and a Democratic Congress to find out how much of this strange little campaign can actually become law. Not bad for the guy who wasn't supposed to get past Iowa.` ]; } return [ `${kEV} electoral votes to ${rEV}. That's it. That's the presidency. Don't let anybody tell you it doesn't count, Dennis, because the Constitution doesn't award bonus points for making the networks comfortable. ${vpVictoryLine(tier)} Nobody is going to call this a sweeping mandate, and half the country is going to wake up tomorrow wondering how in God's name Dennis Kucinich became President. The other half may be wondering the same thing, just more happily.`, `${esc(oppName())} came painfully close. ${variableWeakness(false)} ${OPP_FAIL[oppKey()]||""} A different speech here, a slightly better debate there, and we're probably having a much less enjoyable conversation. Instead, ${esc(oppName())} gets to spend the rest of his life knowing that he came within touching distance of the White House and lost it to the Congressman everybody used to make UFO jokes about.`, `Your political capital isn't unlimited. But you're still going to put your hand on a Bible in January and take the oath of office. You spent this campaign arguing that political courage mattered more than conventional wisdom. Now you get four years to prove it wasn't just something that sounded good on a bumper sticker.` ]; } function lossMargin(kEV,rEV){ if(kEV>=260)return `You finished with ${kEV} electoral votes to ${rEV}. The irony is that President Kucinich has proved considerably less interested in their reassurance than Candidate Kucinich appeared to be.`; } if(v==="gravel")return `Choosing Mike Gravel seemed almost a guarantee that a Kucinich administration would resist Washington's instinct for accommodation, which makes the retreats of the past year particularly difficult to explain.`; if(v==="lee")return `Choosing Barbara Lee appeared to promise an administration that would rather endure isolation than abandon a position it believed morally necessary. He never did. One year into his presidency, he has used executive authority aggressively on criminal justice and civil liberties, begun dismantling some of the ugliest machinery inherited from the Bush years, and opened direct dialogue with governments in Cuba and Venezuela that Washington has spent decades treating as useful enemies. These are not revolutionary acts. They merely appear revolutionary in a political culture where acknowledging the humanity of an adversary is treated as capitulation.`, `Kucinich's supporters should not mistake courage for complete success. His promised Department of Peace exists as a pale shadow of what he envisioned. Republicans speak confidently of a great pendulum swinging back in 2010, and perhaps it will. Entrenched power does not quietly accept even modest challenges to its authority. But Kucinich has expanded the boundaries of what Americans are permitted to imagine their government doing. Whether his presidency ultimately succeeds is unknowable. After one year, however, those who dismissed Dennis Kucinich as a harmless eccentric must confront an uncomfortable fact: he meant it.` ] }; } return { kind:"column", image:IMG.moderate, kicker:"The Nation", title:"What Happened to Dennis Kucinich?", byline:"Chris Hedges · 2010", paragraphs:[ `${vpHedgesOpening(false)} Those of us who defended Kucinich did not do so because we believed he possessed some supernatural immunity to political reality. We defended him because, for decades, he was willing to say what political reality was designed to prevent politicians from saying. A year into his presidency, that distinction has become increasingly difficult to recognize. Immediate withdrawal from Iraq became a timetable, then negotiations, then another promise that withdrawal must be conducted "responsibly." His pledge to remake NAFTA has become a pledge to "renegotiate" it, with precious little renegotiating actually accomplished.`, `Healthcare is more painful still. The defining domestic promise of Kucinich's political life—universal healthcare—is nowhere in sight. Congress produced a badly diluted bill after months of bargaining, only for the Senate to kill even that. The administration insists that the fight is not over. Perhaps it isn't. But presidents eventually discover that asking supporters to celebrate what they attempted is a poor substitute for delivering what they promised. The more serious danger is that a politician elected because Americans believed he would challenge the boundaries of acceptable politics has begun allowing those boundaries to define him.`, `Republicans smell blood. Their leaders openly predict a violent swing of the pendulum in the midterms, while Democrats increasingly behave as though survival depends upon apologizing for having won the last election. Yet I am not prepared to write Dennis Kucinich's political obituary. This is, after all, the man who became the youngest mayor of a major American city, was driven from office amid catastrophe, and lived long enough to see Cleveland vindicate the fight that destroyed him. Perhaps the first year has taught him the true dimensions of the forces arrayed against him. There is still time for Dennis Kucinich to find his way again—to remember why people entrusted him with this office, and to bring this country into the new era he once had the courage to imagine.` ] }; } function crowderSlide(){ return { kind:"crowder",image:IMG.crowder, title:"RED VALENTINE: Comrade Cupid Comes to the Kucinich White House!", byline:"Steven Crowder | PJTV · February 14, 2009", paragraphs:[ `So apparently Valentine's Day at the Kucinich White House looks a little different. First Lady Elizabeth Kucinich posted a perfectly innocent message yesterday about how much she loves her husband, along with a photograph of the two of them and some mushy stuff about how "love is something we create together." Cute, right? Sure. Adorable. Except—and maybe I'm the crazy one here—does anybody else notice that even the Kuciniches can't talk about love without making it sound collectivist? Whatever happened to I love my husband? Nope. Love is something "we create together." Presumably through a federally administered Department of Romance, where every American is guaranteed an equal share of affection regardless of whether they've actually earned it. Somewhere right now, Dennis Kucinich is probably drafting legislation to seize excess Valentine's chocolates from productive boyfriends and redistribute them to the dateless. Although judging by these two, I'm starting to suspect Elizabeth is the one who wears the pants in the First Family. Dennis might be President of the United States, but something tells me he's still asking the First Lady whether he's allowed to have another piece of chocolate.`, `And before the emails start: yes, I'M JOKING. Mostly. Elizabeth's message is sweet, Dennis clearly adores his wife, and good for them. But that's what makes the Kucinich presidency so bizarrely entertaining. This is a president who can make a romantic Valentine's Day photo look like the cover of a pamphlet called Workers of the World, Cuddle! Of course, while the First Couple celebrates their love, President Kucinich is busy worrying about showing a little love to the guys down at Guantánamo Bay, where he apparently can't release prisoners quickly enough. Maybe next February Gitmo detainees get federally subsidized Valentine's cards too. I'm sure tonight Dennis and Elizabeth will enjoy a lovely candlelit dinner—locally grown vegetables, union-made candles, and one entrée divided equally between them in solidarity with the proletariat. Happy Valentine's Day, Mr. President. Just remember: you can share your heart with Elizabeth. You don't have to share my paycheck with everybody else—and you definitely don't have to share my country with the guys from Gitmo.` ], cta:`Link to new video BELOW! It was widely panned, crude, barely coherent and almost impossible to describe as a movie because there was no real plot — just four separate sketches in which animated Dennis and Ron wandered into increasingly ridiculous situations and somehow got themselves back out. Five years later, it has become a genuine sleeper cult hit, dissected in political-science courses, animation classes and by people who simply cannot believe it exists. The humor feels less like anything normally airing on cable after 10 p.m. than a lost SCTV sketch somebody accidentally stretched to half an hour. Lewis Black and the late George Carlin lending their voices to several bits certainly helped, but the real attraction is how completely unaware the two candidates sound of what they are participating in.`, `Everybody remembers the bald-eagle sketch, where Paul tries to feed the eagle's babies by chewing stale crackers and spitting them into their mouths, only for the mother to return and peck his eyes out. But the polar-bear segment may be even better. Kucinich ends up riding a melting glacier and announces, with total sincerity, "I knew fighting climate change would get slippery, but frankly, this is just ridiculous." It is written like a joke and delivered by Dennis as though he is explaining a municipal bond issue. That accidental seriousness is the secret ingredient. Neither man sounds like he has the slightest idea what the hell he is making, and the cartoon becomes funnier every time the script expects them to. R&D Save America is awful in exactly the right way: bizarre, sincere, cheap-looking and utterly unlike any campaign artifact before or since. Put their politics aside for 27 minutes and Kucinich and Paul somehow made something genuinely special — even if we're still not convinced either of them knew it at the time.` ] }; } function color:#fff!important; border:1px solid #9299a4!important; border-radius:4px!important; padding:6px 10px!important; font:700 11px Arial,sans-serif!important; cursor:pointer!important; box-shadow:0 2px 7px rgba(0,0,0,.4)!important; } #k08-ach-gallery{ position:fixed!important; inset:8% 10%!important; z-index:2147483646!important; background:rgba(24,27,32,.985)!important; border:2px solid #737b87!important; border-radius:6px!important; padding:14px!important; box-sizing:border-box!important; overflow-y:auto!important; color:#fff!important; font-family:Arial,sans-serif!important; box-shadow:0 7px 28px rgba(0,0,0,.7)!important; } #k08-ach-gallery .k08-ach-head{ display:flex!important;justify-content:space-between!important;align-items:center!important; margin-bottom:12px!important; } #k08-ach-gallery h2{margin:0!important;color:#fff!important;font:800 22px Arial,sans-serif!important;} #k08-ach-gallery-close{ background:#555d68!important;color:#fff!important;border:1px solid #8d96a2!important; padding:5px 10px!important;cursor:pointer!important;font-weight:700!important; } #k08-ach-gallery-grid{ display:grid!important; grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(235px,1fr))!important; gap:9px!important; } .k08-ach-gallery-card{ display:flex!important;gap:9px!important;align-items:center!important; padding:8px!important;background:#343941!important;border:1px solid #555d68!important; min-height:74px!important;box-sizing:border-box!important; } .k08-ach-gallery-card.locked{opacity:.42!important;filter:grayscale(1)!important;} .k08-ach-gallery-card img{ width:58px!important;height:58px!important;object-fit:cover!important;flex:0 0 58px!important; } .k08-ach-gallery-card b{display:block!important;color:#fff!important;font-size:13px!important;} .k08-ach-gallery-card small{display:block!important;color:#d2d6dc!important;font-size:11px!important;margin-top:3px!important;} .k08-ach-gallery-card .status{font-size:9px!important;text-transform:uppercase!important;letter-spacing:.5px!important;margin-top:4px!important;color:#a9bcff!important;} `; document.head.appendChild(st); function openGallery(){ document.getElementById("k08-ach-gallery")?.remove(); const unlocked=unlockedSet(); const panel=document.createElement("div"); panel.id="k08-ach-gallery"; panel.innerHTML=`

Achievements

${ITEMS.map(([id,title,desc,img])=>`
${title} ${desc}
${unlocked.has(id)?"Unlocked":"Locked"}
`).join("")}
`; document.body.appendChild(panel); panel.querySelector("#k08-ach-gallery-close").onclick=()=>panel.remove(); } function installButton(){ if(document.getElementById("k08-ach-gallery-button"))return; const b=document.createElement("button"); b.id="k08-ach-gallery-button"; b.type="button"; b.textContent="Achievements"; b.onclick=openGallery; document.body.appendChild(b); } installButton(); if(!document.body)setTimeout(installButton,50); })();
